Here are your assigned scenarios and the guidance, please implement or ask questions.

- Scenarios: the Gherkin block of /home/vscode/rebaseline/features/feat-tool-skills-rest.md — the sixteen scenarios tagged @bounded-context:shopsystem-product (the lead shop's own tree, /home/vscode/rebaseline).
- Guidance: /home/vscode/rebaseline/guidance/feat-tool-skills-rest-shopsystem-product.md.

Working rules of this tree: work in /home/vscode/rebaseline on the rebaseline branch; do not commit (the lead-pm commits); use `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` or /home/vscode/.claude/jobs/71c24a0e/tmp for scratch files, not /tmp; run `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` before you report and report its last line; do not use these words: ratif, disposition, rebaseline bill, surface, seat. When done, report what you changed (each file with its version), what each scenario's Then shows in the running tree with the command that shows it, and anything you could not do and why. If something the scenarios and guidance do not say is needed, ask by returning the question with the default you would apply.

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- adr-authoring: Author one architecture decision record from a decision the solutions architect role or the authority has taken, and check it against the adr fitness set and the architecture principle set, so that the PM role rules from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion named, or a definition change — and the decision bounds nothing until the record is checked. Use when an architecture decision — stack, guardrail, decomposition, contract, or non-functional requirement — has been taken or must be taken and needs its record authored, screened, and ruled on.
- backlog-ordering: Place a planned initiative's features-to-be in the backlog order: the PO role writes the superseding order against the PM role's recorded priority — enabler recommendations placed or declined with reasons — and the PO output check sets its status. Use when a planned initiative must be placed in the backlog order and the order checked.
- corpus-close-out: Execute the migration plan's pre-decided retire and terminal actions mechanically, at cut-over: snapshot the corpus, delete the terminal trees, move each run's retired rows to the archive, regenerate the scenario refs, verify every actioned row landed where its action says, and finally promote the migration branch to `main`.
- definition-chain-migration: Convert one artifact type from the frozen corpus into the new baseline: build its definition chain, prove the chain on a real keeper, approve it, rewrite every keeper through it, and move what does not survive to the archive.
- discovery-conversation: Conduct a bounded discovery dialogue in a declared form — brainstorm (the first form), interview, or review of evidence — opened on a topic, or on a request routed to it: the authority explores direction with the lead-pm as interlocutor, nothing is operationalized before convergence, the session record anchors the conversation, and a converged discovery leaves an initiative recorded `proposed` — or `proposed` and then `cancelled` in the same document when what was asked is declined, so the record of the decline survives.
- feature-authoring: Author one feature from a planned initiative and take it through its check: the PO role writes it alone from the initiative's framing, the product designer and solutions architect roles add the criteria that ride on its scenarios, and the PO output check sets its status. Use when a planned initiative needs one more feature authored, the designer's and architect's criteria added, and the check run.
- initiative-check: Take a proposed initiative to the bet: the solutions architect and product designer roles attach the sections they own, each decision the solutions architect role's offer leaves unrecorded is recorded through the ADR authoring process before the screen, the cold reviewer screens the whole against the initiative fitness set — the check of record on the PM role's framing — and the authority decides, from the verdict, whether to spend the appetite. Use when a proposed initiative needs its feasibility, decomposition, and usability attached, the check of record run, and the authority's bet taken.
- lint-basis: The lint over the lead shop's definition corpus: checks the basis tree and the request, brief, and guidance records at the repository root against their typedefs' rules, derives an artifact type's definition chain from the references its documents carry, and checks one decision brief or one process definition alone. Use it before reporting any change to the tree, after editing a definition, brief, request, or guidance record, when a process definition names a tool, and when an artifact type's chain is wanted; it changes no file. Tool: `basis/tools/lint_basis.py`. Uses, each with its exact invocation below: `lint`, `check-brief`, `check-process`, `derive-chain`.
- po-output-check: Check a piece of the PO role's output against the PM role's framing under criteria the definitions state, so that the PM role decides from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion named, or a definition change — and never by reading every artifact. Use when the PO role submits a feature, product decision record, or backlog order for the PM role's check against the framing.
- principle-set-authoring: Author or amend a principle set: the author drafts through the guideline, an independent fresh-context judge scores the draft against the fitness set, and the set enters force only by the owner's approval. Use when authoring or amending a principle set.
- product-flow: Carry one problem from discovery to assigned work: a discovery conversation frames an initiative, the initiative check takes it to the authority's bet, the backlog ordering places it, and the flow then loops — one feature authored, checked, and its scenarios assigned — until the PO role judges the initiative's features done. The shop's operating process; every sub-process is defined in its own document.
- reconcile-and-close: Convert a BC's completed dispatch into reconciled shop state: the response consumed, the work item closed with a traceable reason, the scenario contract confirmed, and follow-ups filed.
- request-intake: Take an ask — one expression of intent brought to the lead shop by an originator — from the words it arose in to a request recorded in the repository and routed by the lead-pm role: the originator confirms that the words make an ask before anything is recorded, the request records the words verbatim with the date, the lead-pm decides the route — a discovery conversation, the small-change lane, or a decline settled with the product authority — and says it with its reason before it is acted on, and the run returns the request carrying its route and, once the destination exists, where the route led. Use when words that may be an ask reach the lead shop — brought directly, arising in open conversation, or arising during a run of another process — and no request records them yet; or a request stands recorded with its route awaiting and the lead-pm role is to route it.
- research-inquiry: Answer a question with a research report: the researcher frames and plans, gathers in parallel, extracts grounded evidence, synthesizes findings with confidence and alternatives, verifies the claims in a fresh context, and delivers a report the consumer can act on — stored on the `research` branch and registered in the research index. Use when a question needs an answer with sourced, confidence-labeled findings the asker can act on.
- review-conversation: Conduct a bounded review: the authority examines material and issues decisions; each decision is applied as changes to the affected artifacts before the next exchange; the conversation ends only when the authority closes or cancels it, and parks itself on inactivity.
- role-rendering: Make every approved role definition of the lead shop available at the agent's load point — the `.claude/agents/` directory the harness instantiates subagents from — by checking what stands there against a fresh render of each approved definition and reconciling every difference through the compiler, so that an agent filling a named role in a process step operates from the approved definition of that role: placement at the load point is what makes the role instantiable, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that every approved role is available. Use when an approved role definition changes or lands, a role at the agent's load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its definition, or left by a definition no longer approved — or the shop must confirm that every approved role is available.
- scenario-assignment: Turn a checked feature into work the Bounded Context shops can take up: the solutions architect role tags each scenario with the context that owns its behavior, reads each tagged context's pre-state, sweeps the feature repository for conflicts, records the feature as assigned, and sends each shop its scenarios as an `assign_scenarios` message. Use when a feature has passed the PO output check and its scenarios must each be assigned to the Bounded Context that owns the behavior and sent to that shop.
- session-handoff: Close a conversation so later work starts from governed records alone — no memory channel, no chat summary, and no transcript as the carrier.
- skill-rendering: Make every approved process definition of the lead shop, and every framework tool of the lead shop that answers the standard question, available at the agent's load point — the `.claude/skills/` directory the harness loads skills from — by checking what stands there against a fresh render of each approved definition and a fresh production from each tool's answer, and reconciling every difference through the compiler of that source kind, so that an agent beginning an activity operates from the approved definition of that activity and an agent running a tool operates from what the tool now says about itself: placement at the load point is what makes the skill load, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that every approved process and every answering tool is available. Use when an approved process definition changes or lands, a framework tool's answer to the standard question changes or a tool begins to answer, a loadable skill at the agent's load point stands in doubt — missing, hand-edited, not current with its tool's answer, or left by a definition no longer approved — or the shop must confirm that every approved process and every answering tool is available.
- small-change: Take a request whose route is the small-change lane to a verified result. No bet is taken and no check of record is run in this process: both protect the appetite an initiative's bet spends (the [initiative typedef](../artifacts/initiative.md)'s term), and a simple change — the glossary's term — spends none of it worth a bet. Use when a request's route is small-change and its work item stands — the lead shop is to take the simple change it records to a verified result; never for an ask not yet recorded as a request, and never in place of the request-intake process's routing.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use when before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- typedef-rendering: Keep the two texts of every artifact type current with the type's one standard. The process checks what stands at the two load points against a fresh render of each qualifying typedef by the *compiler* — the tool of the *lead shop*, this repository, the shop that owns the product's definitions — that produces both texts from a typedef, and reconciles every difference through the compiler — so that a maker and a checker of the type work from the same words, a change to the typedef reaches both texts, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that they do. Use when an approved typedef carrying its writing rules and fitness scenarios changes or lands, a guideline or fitness set at its load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its typedef, written by hand, or left by a typedef that no longer qualifies — or the shop must confirm that every such typedef has both of its texts current.
- work-conversation: Conduct a bounded operational discussion scoped to one work item: every exchange lands on the item, so the discussion is containable, findable, and survives the transcript.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Working principles (compiled into every session)

These statements govern every activity in this shop. The full set —
rationales, implications, fitness screen — is the source document
named in the front-matter; on conflict the source wins.

- **Define what good looks like up front** (`define-good-up-front`):
  - Every activity MUST operate from a stated definition of what good looks like.
  - That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and its check.
  - The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability.
  - Whoever makes an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check.
  - That evaluation MUST be recorded with the output — in its Document History or the step's own output.
- **Govern the generating context** (`governed-context`):
  - Everything loaded into an agent's generating context — prompts, skills, memories, primers — MUST trace to an approved definition or a governed record.
  - An unsanctioned context channel MUST NOT be created or retained.
- **Every activity belongs to a process** (`no-orphan-activities`):
  - Every activity in the system MUST be part of a defined process with stated expected outcomes, expected outputs, and possible resulting actions.
  - Every long-running loop MUST declare its exit — a reached-state success exit, a round or budget cap, or both.
- **Use defined terms** (`use-defined-terms`):
  - Important terms MUST be defined in the system, in the glossary or as a schema element.
  - A term is important when a reader must know it to perform or check the work.
  - When more than one term could carry a statement, the writer MUST use a defined term if one is available.
- **Use external standards first** (`external-standards-first`):
  - A definition MUST adopt an established external form where one fits.
  - Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it rejects.
- **Single source of truth** (`single-source-of-truth`):
  - Every fact, rule, or definition MUST have exactly one authoritative home.
  - Every other appearance MUST be a reference or a generated rendering.
- **Feedback loops have consumers** (`feedback-loops-with-consumers`):
  - Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting action.
  - The effectiveness of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be measured.
  - The definitions of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be updated from what is measured.
- **Delivery is verified in the running system** (`delivery-verified`):
  - Work MUST be counted done only when its effect is demonstrated in the running system.
  - Artifacts existing, checks passing, or reviews approving MUST NOT count as done on their own.
- **Load the least context** (`least-context`):
  - An activity MUST load the minimum context necessary to accomplish its task.
  - The activity's process MUST name what loads into context and the source each input comes from.
  - Context from an unapproved source MUST NOT be loaded.
- **Use tools through skills** (`tools-through-skills`):
  - Every framework tool MUST be usable through a skill that states, for each use it supports, what it does, what it takes, what it returns, and how it fails, so that an agent uses it without reading its help.
  - An agent MUST prefer that skill over a bare invocation of the tool.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST be recorded as a gap.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST NOT be worked around.

# Rebaseline migration branch — session primer

The product is the **shopsystem**: the system by which a lead shop
and its Bounded Context shops — agent-run execution units — take a
problem from discovery to verified, running software; it is built by
the same kind of shops it defines, and this repository is its lead
shop. For whom: the people who stand up and run products on it — a
product authority who frames and bets, and the builders and operators
who meet the work through its interaction types. The shop's operating
process is
[product-flow](../../basis/processes/product-flow.md): discovery →
initiative check and bet → backlog ordering → feature authoring →
scenario assignment, each stage a defined sub-process with its own
check.

This is the `rebaseline` branch: the greenfield tree of the
shopsystem-product migration, seeded 2026-08-22 under the approved
migration plan. Nothing exists here except through an explicit import
step; nothing from the old corpus is read here except through the
curated feed.

## Governing instruments

- `basis/` on this branch — the definition corpus. Every activity here
  operates through these definitions; the index is
  [`basis/README.md`](../../basis/README.md).
- The migration plan: `main:drafts/migration-plan.md` (read via
  `git show`; reference only) — phases, entry conditions, action table.
- The frozen corpus: `main` — the BC shops' contract of record until
  cut-over, and the pre-migration reference. Never copy from it outside
  an import step or the curated feed. The branch pulls from `main`;
  `main` never publishes to the branch.

## Current state

Seed and Phase 0 are complete: both principle sets stand approved.
Phase 1: the meta-chains, the four lead-shop roles, the ask mechanism
(held-and-resumed only), and the experience guidance corpus stand
approved. The product flow is defined end to end and approved by
batch under brief-032: `discovery-conversation` (brainstorm,
interview, or review of evidence; frames the initiative) →
`initiative-check` (attach, screen as check of record, the
authority's bet) → `backlog-ordering` → `feature-authoring` (the PO
authors alone; designer criteria and architect constraints ride the
scenarios) → `po-output-check` (activates the initiative on the first
pass) → `scenario-assignment` (repository sweep, `assign_scenarios`
only), with `product-flow` as the top level. The initiative, feature,
backlog-order, and product-decision-record chains are approved. Open:
the reconcile-side amendments (the initiative's `completed` state,
the product changelog, the roadmap, the `router` role); the scenario
register — a feature to be built by integrating the work on `main`;
the designer role's corpus records (vocabulary, patterns, tokens;
core tasks stand as hypotheses); brief-030's role-definition typedef
amendment and the 38-skill import plan.

## Operating rules

- The shop is frozen: no dispatches, no mailbox work; BC responses
  queue on `main`'s infrastructure until post-migration.
- Work proceeds by phase: Phase 0 (architecture principles) → Phase 1
  (meta-chains, then PM/PO/Architect definitions) → Phase 2
  (progressive disclosure as the first feature) → Phase 3 (demand-pull
  corpus migration, one discovery interview per feature).
- The product authority decides at every chain-and-exemplar step and
  phase exit; deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go
  through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions.
- Decisions are applied as changes to the affected definitions and
  recorded in their Document History; no decision ledger exists, and no
  document cites one as authority.
- Session close: work is not done until `git push` succeeds on this
  branch.

# Memory index

- [PM dialogue before operationalizing](pm-dialogue-before-operationalizing.md) — David's mode correction: in deciding/discovery conversations, engage his statements as an interlocutor; record and launch only after convergence.
- [SAFe stance](safe-framework-stance.md) — David finds SAFe over-complicated; cite it as one position, never adopt it as a model.
- [David fills lead-pm](david-fills-lead-pm.md) — David is lead-pm himself, agent-assisted, daily review budget; lead-po is the maker he checks.

13	# Feature: Tool skills for the rest
14	
15	## Feature
16	
17	Feature: Tool skills for the rest
18	  Every agent of the shop that runs a tool, and the shops whose tools
19	  the product accepts,
20	  can use each of the other eleven framework tools — the five
21	  compilers the shop owns and the six tools it runs but does not own —
22	  through a skill that states, for each use it supports, what it does,
23	  what it takes, what it returns, and how it fails: the skill produced
24	  from what the tool says about itself in answer to the one standard
25	  question, or, for a tool that cannot answer, from a description
26	  beside it in the same shape until its owner answers,
27	  so that every framework tool is usable through a skill produced
28	  from the tool's own answer — a tool from any shop is usable the
29	  moment it answers, a tool that cannot answer has a description
30	  beside it in the same shape, and a change to what a tool says about
31	  itself reaches its skill.
32	
33	## Contributors
34	
35	Owning shop, per scenario — from the initiative's Decomposition
36	section, which names no Bounded Context: every change sits in the
37	lead shop's tree, no contract exists on this branch, and the
38	cross-context flow is none. The six external tools are owned by other
39	shops, and each description beside one names that owner as the gap's
40	addressee; the scenarios that write the descriptions, produce the
41	skills, and record the gaps are the lead shop's, the shop that runs
42	the tools, as the decision the bet rests on places them.
43	
44	- *a compiler the shop owns answers the standard question* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
45	- *a compiler's skill is produced from the compiler's own answer* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
46	- *the producer of tool skills produces its own skill from its own answer* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
47	- *a tool that cannot answer has a description beside it in the same shape* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
48	- *a description beside a tool that is not in the answer's shape yields no skill* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
49	- *the skill of a tool that cannot answer is produced from the description beside it* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
50	- *a tool that cannot answer is recorded as a gap against its owner* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
51	- *each use entry in a produced skill is complete* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
52	- *a change to what a compiler says about itself reaches its skill* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
53	- *a change to the description beside a tool reaches its skill* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
54	- *a tool skill not current with the description beside its tool is reported* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
55	- *a tool that begins to answer is used through its answer, not the description beside it* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
56	- *the check over the load point passes clean with every tool's skill in place* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
57	- *a tool's skill is loaded for a task that calls for the tool* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
58	- *an agent completes a use of a tool on the first invocation the skill states* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
59	- *a failure the agent meets is one the skill names, read as the skill states it* — shopsystem-product (the lead shop)
60	
61	Vocabulary. Terms defined in the Contributors section of
62	[feat-tool-skills](feat-tool-skills.md), used here with that
63	section's meaning and read of any tool where it reads of the lint —
64	one clause each to read by, the definition staying that feature's:
65	**framework tool** — a tool the shop's definitions name for an
66	activity; **skill** — the rendering at the agent's load point that
67	states a tool's use so an agent performs it from the skill alone;
68	**gap** — a missing definition, tool, or skill the shop records
69	rather than works around; **the standard question** — the one
70	question every framework tool is asked about itself, the same for a
71	tool from any shop; **the answer** — what a tool says in reply: its
72	name, what it does, one use entry per use; **use**, **use entry** —
73	one thing a tool can be asked to do, and its entry of four parts
74	with, in the skill, the exact invocation; **a part of its own** — a
75	part present as itself, not inferred from another; **produced from**
76	— a rendering of its source, never edited by hand and never the
77	source; **current with** — what a fresh production from the source as
78	it now stands would yield; **the process that keeps tool skills
79	current** — the process whose run produces each tool skill afresh
80	from its source; **the check over tool skills** — that process's
81	check, reporting a skill not current; **the agent's load point** —
82	where the agent runtime loads skills from; **the check over the load
83	point** — the check feat-skills-availability specifies there; **a
84	fresh context**, **its only source on a tool** — an agent whose
85	context holds the tool's skill and nothing else about the tool; **the
86	first invocation** — the first command the agent issues to the tool
87	for a use; **a bare invocation** — the tool run other than as its
88	skill states; **a stable code** — a failure's identifier, the same on
89	every run that fails the same way. Terms this feature adds, in the
90	order the scenarios use them:
91	
92	- **the five compilers the shop owns** — the framework tools under
93	  the lead shop's tools directory other than the lint: the four that
94	  render a definition into its produced text (a principle set, a
95	  typedef, a process, a role) and **the producer of tool skills** —
96	  the compiler that asks a tool the standard question and produces
97	  its skill from the answer, itself a framework tool that must answer
98	  (the initiative's Document History v11; the architect's second risk,
99	  v3). "A compiler" in a scenario is any one of the five, and a
100	  scenario over a compiler is read once per compiler.
101	- **a tool the shop runs but does not own**, **the six external
102	  tools** — bd (the work register), shop-msg, shop-knowledge,
103	  agent-vault, bc-emit, shop-templates (the initiative's Document
104	  History v11; the discovery's evidence table, sess-2026-09-06-c):
105	  framework tools named in the shop's definitions or used by hand,
106	  owned by other shops, none of which answers the standard question
107	  today. "A tool that cannot answer" in a scenario is any one of the
108	  six, and a scenario over one is read once per tool.
109	- **the owner of a tool** — the shop that owns the tool: the shop
110	  that can make it answer the standard question, and the addressee of
111	  the gap recorded while it does not.
112	- **a description beside a tool** — the framing's "description beside
113	  it in the same shape": what a tool that cannot answer would say
114	  about itself, written by the shop that runs the tool in the shape an
115	  answer takes — the tool's name, what it does, and one use entry per
116	  use with its four parts — naming the tool it stands beside and that
117	  tool's owner; the source of that tool's skill until the tool
118	  answers, when the answer replaces it. "For each use it supports",
119	  read of a description (the designer's question, ruled at the
120	  check): at least every use of the tool a shop definition or a
121	  load-point skill names and every use the shop runs by hand; a use
122	  outside that is described when a task first calls for it, never
123	  run bare. Where a description is written from is a rule on its
124	  writer, constraint (7).
125	- **the same shape** — the shape an answer takes, one shape for every
126	  tool from any shop; the decision the bet rests on,
127	  [adr-2026-09-07-tool-answer](../decisions/adr-2026-09-07-tool-answer.md)
128	  (checked), fixes it, and the scenarios name only its parts.
129	- **what the tool says about itself** — for a tool that answers, its
130	  answer; for a tool that cannot answer, the description beside it,
131	  standing in the answer's place until the tool answers. "Current
132	  with" is read against this: a change to the answer, or to the
133	  description, since the skill was produced leaves a skill that is
134	  not current. **The tool's source**, wherever it appears in this
135	  document, means the program's source — what the
136	  tools-through-skills principle forbids an agent to read — and never
137	  the answer or the description.
138	- **the measure** — the initiative's: framework tools usable through
139	  a skill produced from the tool's own answer. Now 1 of 12, the lint;
140	  after this feature 6 of 12 — the lint and the five compilers. The
141	  six external tools are usable through a skill produced from the
142	  description beside each and are not counted until their owners
143	  answer (the PM role's ruling at the check; the count is that role's
144	  to read).
145	
146	Provenance of the scenarios, outside the ownership list: *the
147	producer of tool skills produces its own skill from its own answer* —
148	the initiative's Document History v11 and the architect's second risk
149	(v3), the producer a framework tool that counts in the measure; *a
150	description beside a tool that is not in the answer's shape yields no
151	skill* and *a tool skill not current with the description beside its
152	tool is reported* — the architect's fourth risk (v3), what a check
153	can reach of a hand-written description, the rest an Edges row; *a
154	tool that begins to answer is used through its answer, not the
155	description beside it* — the framing's "usable the moment it answers"
156	and the Appetite's "until their owners answer"; *a tool that cannot
157	answer is recorded as a gap against its owner* — the stand-in part of
158	the decision the bet rests on, in scope by the PM role's ruling at
159	the check, the authority's "until their owners answer" presupposing
160	it; the last three scenarios — the designer's usability acceptance
161	criteria (a)–(c) (the initiative's Document History v5), read of any
162	of the eleven. The For whom section names no interaction type and
163	the Decomposition no Bounded Context; what criteria are due, the
164	designer's and the architect's passages below record.
165	
166	The product designer role's criteria (feature-authoring's
167	add-usability step, 2026-09-07):
168	
169	*Due: none.* The For whom section's "none" holds against the
170	core-task list (v4): no core task carries a tool skill, a tool's
171	answer, or a description beside a tool. Four interfaces are delivered
172	regardless and screened under `agent-is-a-user` — each tool's skill
173	(`api`), each compiler's answer (`cli`), the producer's report to a
174	description's writer (`cli`), and the gap record as its owner reads
175	it — so the criteria below stand, each a hypothesis under
176	`evidence-not-opinion` until observed as measured task completion in
177	the delivery; the reasoning, the accessibility reasoning, and the
178	delivery screen's routing are in this document's history (v2, v4).
179	
180	Usability acceptance criteria, riding on the scenarios by name, no
181	scenario text changed — (a)–(c) feat-tool-skills' read of any of the
182	eleven, (d) and (e) this feature's own:
183	
184	- (a) *the first invocation is the skill's* — rides on *an agent
185	  completes a use of a tool on the first invocation the skill states*
186	  and *a tool's skill is loaded for a task that calls for the tool*.
187	  Met, per tool, when the agent's first command to the tool for a use
188	  is the invocation the skill states and the use completes with the
189	  return the skill states; read once per tool on at least one use the
190	  skill states — for a tool whose uses the freeze bars, on a use it
191	  allows, or "hypothesis" for that tool in the delivery. Invalidated
192	  by a read of the tool's source, its help, its answer, or the
193	  description beside it; a second attempt; or a bare invocation with
194	  the skill present.
195	- (b) *each use entry is complete* — rides on *each use entry in a
196	  produced skill is complete* and, as its test in use, *a failure the
197	  agent meets is one the skill names, read as the skill states it*.
198	  Met when every use entry of every produced skill carries the five
199	  parts the scenario states and the failing run's failure is one its
200	  entry names, read from the skill alone; read at least once over the
201	  eleven and at least once on a skill produced from a description —
202	  there a failure the skill does not name is the description's drift
203	  observed (the Edges row on drift). Invalidated by a failure the
204	  skill does not name, or a part inferred from another rather than
205	  present.
206	- (c) *the skill is offered for the task* — rides on *a tool's skill
207	  is loaded for a task that calls for the tool*. Met when, in a fresh
208	  context with the twelve tool skills at the load point, the skill of
209	  the tool the task calls for is loaded before any invocation.
210	  Invalidated by a bare invocation with the skill present, or by
211	  another tool's skill loaded in its place; the remedy for either is
212	  the producer's, not a scenario.
213	- (d) *the lack is reported for the writer* — rides on *a description
214	  beside a tool that is not in the answer's shape yields no skill*
215	  and *the producer of tool skills produces its own skill from its own
216	  answer*. Met when the report names the tool and the part (the
217	  vocabulary's word or its recorded api mapping), gives the next
218	  step, and carries a stable code beside that and not in place of it —
219	  and the failure is one the producer's own skill names, so the writer
220	  reads it from that skill alone. Invalidated by a traceback, a
221	  parser's message, or a schema path standing in place of the part;
222	  by the part named without the tool; or by a failure on a
223	  description that the producer's skill does not name.
224	- (e) *the gap is actionable by its owner* — rides on *a tool that
225	  cannot answer is recorded as a gap against its owner*. Met when the
226	  record, read by the owning shop with nothing else, states in its
227	  first line what happened — the tool does not answer the standard
228	  question — and, as its one action, what answering takes: the
229	  standard question and where its shape is published. Invalidated by
230	  a record from which the owner must ask what to answer or in what
231	  shape. A hypothesis until a gap reaches an owner after the freeze
232	  (the Edges row on it), and the delivery says so.
233	
234	*Accessibility criteria: none due* — no type is named; the skill is
235	agent-facing under `agent-is-a-user`, so no WCAG target applies to
236	it; the compilers' answers and the producer's report are `cli`
237	interactions whose WCAG2ICT applicability record is written once for
238	the type at the delivery screen; the description is a file its writer
239	edits in their own editor; the gap record's accessibility is the
240	request lane's record's. No criterion names an output's form (Edges
241	row added). The delivery screen of the four interfaces under the
242	interaction-conformance-check process is a gate the Edges table holds,
243	not a criterion.
244	
245	The solutions architect role's constraints (feature-authoring's
246	add-constraints step, 2026-09-07):
247	
248	*Contract bound: none; cross-context flow: none.* The initiative's
249	Decomposition section (v12) names no Bounded Context, no contract
250	exists on this branch, and none of the six tools' owners is relied on
251	by contract — what the lead shop holds about each is its own
252	description, under (7); every scenario stays the lead shop's.
253	*Guardrail: one, and it binds.* The decision the bet rests on,
254	[adr-2026-09-07-tool-answer](../decisions/adr-2026-09-07-tool-answer.md)
255	(checked, v3), whose §2, §3 fourth consequence, and bound on Bounded
256	Context shops reach every one of the eleven as they reached the lint.
257	Nine constraints — what must hold, not how; the how is the maker's
258	within them, and a choice outside them is a question against the
259	record: (1)–(6) the first feature's read of any of the eleven, each
260	with what this feature adds; (7)–(9) this feature's own. Each rides
261	on scenarios by name; no scenario text changed by this role. The
262	pre-state read for them and their screen against the architecture
263	principle set are in this document's history (v3, v4).
264	
265	- (1) *what counts as an answer* — rides on *a compiler the shop owns
266	  answers the standard question*, read once per compiler, *the
267	  producer of tool skills produces its own skill from its own answer*,
268	  and *a tool that begins to answer is used through its answer, not
269	  the description beside it*. A reply is an answer only as the
270	  record's §2 counts one: given on the standard flag, written to
271	  standard output with exit status 0 before any other action and with
272	  other arguments ignored, parsing against the tool-description data
273	  type; a traceback, a usage sheet, the flag read as a file path, a
274	  rendering performed, another exit status, or output that does not
275	  parse is "cannot answer" and the Then unmet. The producer is one of
276	  the five with no special case. The same line, both observations
277	  made together, decides when a tool a description stands beside has
278	  begun to answer; a reply that fails either leaves it a tool that
279	  cannot answer, and the description stands.
280	- (2) *the shape is the contract's — one shape, the description in it
281	  too* — rides on *a tool that cannot answer has a description beside
282	  it in the same shape*, *a description beside a tool that is not in
283	  the answer's shape yields no skill*, and *each use entry in a
284	  produced skill is complete*. The data type stands approved (v2),
285	  and every answer and every description is read against it. A
286	  description is an instance of that same data type (the record's §2
287	  stand-in part): the same schema block, the same validation, no
288	  relaxed variant for a hand-written file; kept at the one home the
289	  data type names; carrying the two fields the data type reserves for
290	  it — which tool it stands beside, which shop owns that tool — so a
291	  description lacking either is not in the shape and yields no skill;
292	  its name unique among the product's twelve tools, being the skill's
293	  name. The lack is reported by the part's name as the data type fixes
294	  it; the report's wording for its writer is the designer's (d).
295	- (3) *sole source, and the direction of repair* — rides on *a
296	  compiler's skill is produced from the compiler's own answer*, *the
297	  skill of a tool that cannot answer is produced from the description
298	  beside it*, *a change to what a compiler says about itself reaches
299	  its skill*, *a change to the description beside a tool reaches its
300	  skill*, and *a tool skill not current with the description beside
301	  its tool is reported*. For a compiler, as at the lint: the answer is
302	  the sole source; "current with" is decided by asking again and
303	  digesting the fresh answer, never a kept copy, never the program's
304	  source; a difference resolves toward the answer. For a tool that
305	  cannot answer, the file beside it is the source in the same sense:
306	  the digest over the file's bytes as they stand, "current with"
307	  decided by re-producing from the file each run, the skill's
308	  provenance naming the file and, beside it, the tool it stands
309	  beside; a difference resolves toward the file, and a hand-edited
310	  skill does not survive the next production. Drift found in use (the
311	  Edges row on it) is repaired in the description, never in the skill;
312	  the description is the source only until the tool answers.
313	- (4) *the load-point check recognizes, never exempts — three source
314	  kinds now* — rides on *the check over the load point passes clean
315	  with every tool's skill in place*, *a tool skill not current with
316	  the description beside its tool is reported*, and *a tool that
317	  begins to answer is used through its answer, not the description
318	  beside it*. The check reads a skill by its source kind — an approved
319	  process definition, a tool under the shop's tools directory, or a
320	  description at the home the data type names — never by an
321	  exemption, a skip list, or a hand-marked exception; the producer's
322	  own skill is checked through the producer like any tool's. For the
323	  third kind (the record's digest gate; its §3 fourth consequence):
324	  each run re-produces from every description and diffs, reporting a
325	  difference by the tool's name, and asks the tool every description
326	  stands beside — an answer there is the finding the record names, a
327	  second home, resolved by producing the skill from the answer and
328	  retiring the description, never by editing the answer. The
329	  amendment that recognizes the third kind is the process owner's,
330	  raised at skill-rendering v8, in the order the process-definition
331	  typedef's commitment fixes; until it lands the clean-pass Then is
332	  unmet; feat-skills-availability's seven scenarios pass as today.
333	- (5) *the answer's form binds no shop's language* — rides on *a
334	  compiler the shop owns answers the standard question* and *a tool
335	  that cannot answer has a description beside it in the same shape*.
336	  The framed outcome it protects: a tool from any shop is usable the
337	  moment it answers, in whatever language it is written. Every
338	  answer, and every description, is given in the form the record's
339	  JSON bound fixes, and neither answering nor producing a skill from
340	  an answer or a description adds a dependency that binds a shop's
341	  language. A dependency, a vendor, or a recurring cost added by this
342	  feature is the record's delivery read by this role, not a scenario.
343	- (6) *the skill is the artifact of use* — rides on *a tool's skill is
344	  loaded for a task that calls for the tool*, *an agent completes a
345	  use of a tool on the first invocation the skill states*, and *a
346	  failure the agent meets is one the skill names, read as the skill
347	  states it*. The invocation the skill states for a use is the use's
348	  command line as the answer, or the description, gave it, and it is
349	  the invocation whoever performs the step (the record's fifth
350	  consequence). The fresh context's "its only source on that tool"
351	  excludes the description beside a tool as it excludes the answer,
352	  the data type, the program's source, and the help; a use completed
353	  only by reading the description is a skill that does not suffice,
354	  the designer's (a) invalidated — distinct from a use that does not
355	  complete as the skill states, which is the description's drift and
356	  repairs under (3).
357	- (7) *a description is the lead shop's record, not the owner's
358	  contract* — rides on *a tool that cannot answer has a description
359	  beside it in the same shape* and *a tool that cannot answer is
360	  recorded as a gap against its owner*. One description per tool that
361	  cannot answer, naming the tool as the check asks it — the field for
362	  which tool it stands beside carries the invocation the check makes
363	  — and the shop that owns it. It is written from what the tool shows
364	  whoever runs it — its help, its behaviour when run — and never from
365	  the tool's source (the Appetite's second no-go; `knowable-shape`).
366	  Written by the consuming shop about another shop's tool (the
367	  record's bound on Bounded Context shops): no promise in it is owed
368	  by the owner, nothing the lead shop relies on in it is a contract of
369	  the owner's — the relationship kind while the tool does not answer
370	  is conformist; the moment the tool answers, the kind is the
371	  record's, published language and open host service, and the
372	  description is retired.
373	- (8) *the gap's life is the description's* — rides on *a tool that
374	  cannot answer is recorded as a gap against its owner* and *a tool
375	  that begins to answer is used through its answer, not the
376	  description beside it*. One gap per tool, opened when its
377	  description is written and standing while the description is a
378	  skill's source; what it asks is fixed by the record's bound — that
379	  the tool answer the standard flag in the data type's shape — and the
380	  designer's (e) fixes how its owner reads it. It closes on one event
381	  only: the check observing the tool's answer, the skill produced from
382	  it, and the description retired — never by a hand edit, a change to
383	  the description, or a skill written around the tool
384	  (`tools-through-skills`). Its form, ruled at the check on this
385	  role's default: one request record per tool under the request lane,
386	  addressed to the owning shop, held and not routed while the shop is
387	  frozen, naming the tool, its owner, the standard flag, and the data
388	  type; no work item unless the lane asks one. Its reaching the owner
389	  stays out of scope (the Edges row).
390	- (9) *asking is the check's only invocation of an external tool* —
391	  rides on *the check over the load point passes clean with every
392	  tool's skill in place* and *a tool that begins to answer is used
393	  through its answer, not the description beside it*. Under (4) the
394	  check asks each of the six the standard question every run, while
395	  the shop is frozen and the tool is another shop's; a tool that
396	  cannot answer promises nothing about what it does when asked. So
397	  the check asks with the flag alone and no other argument, invokes
398	  the tool for nothing else, and a tool observed to perform a use when
399	  asked is a finding to this role, its asking suspended for that tool
400	  until its owner answers (the Edges row).
401	
402	Enabler work recommended into the PO role's backlog: none new — the
403	one definition change this feature needs, the check's third source
404	kind, is the process owner's amendment already raised at
405	skill-rendering v8 and lands inside this delivery in the order (4)
406	fixes, as the first feature's did.
407	
408	## Interaction types
409	
410	None — a skill is read by an agent inside a process step; no core
411	task carries it (the initiative's For whom section). Recorded at the
412	designer's step and ruled at the check: the description beside a tool
413	that cannot answer is not an interaction type — it is what a person
414	gives the product in the data type's published shape, and the product
415	meets its writer at the producer's command line, which criterion (d)
416	covers; and the gap record another shop will read is a request record
417	the lead shop holds, not an interaction of the product. "None"
418	stands.
